```python
# Where we store the OAuth token once you've logged in once
TOKEN_PATH = BASE_DIR / "youtube_token.pickle"
CLIENT_SECRET_PATH = BASE_DIR / "client_secret_youtube.json"

# YouTube scope for uploading videos
SCOPES = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload"]


# -------- Helpers to find files --------

def find_latest_video() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not VIDEO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    videos = sorted(
        [p for p in VIDEO_DIR.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".mp4"],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return videos[0] if videos else None


def find_latest_meta() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not VIDEO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    metas = sorted(
        [
            p for p in VIDEO_DIR.iterdir()
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".txt"
            and "_YOUTUBE_" in p.name
        ],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return metas[0] if metas else None


def parse_meta_file(meta_path: Path) -> Tuple[str, str, Optional[str]]:
    """
    Expect a structure like:

    Title:
    Some Title Here

    Description:
    Long description...
    (multiple lines)

    Video file:
    somefile.mp4
    """
    text = meta_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def extract_block(label: str) -> str:
        pattern = rf"{label}:\s*(.*?)\n(?:\n|$)"
        # DOTALL so '.' matches newlines; non-greedy so it stops at first blank line
        m = re.search(pattern, text, flags=re.DOTALL)
        if not m:
            return ""
        return m.group(1).strip()

    title = extract_block("Title")
    description = extract_block("Description")
    video_file = extract_block("Video file")

    if not title:
        title = "Untitled Materialist Christianity Video"

    if not description:
        description = (
            "This is part of the ongoing Materialist Christianity project. "
            "We take Christ, the Bible, and the working class seriously."
        )

    return title, description, video_file or None


# -------- YouTube auth & upload --------

def get_authenticated_service():
    """
    Return an authenticated YouTube API client.
    Uses Desktop OAuth. First run will open a browser window.
    """
    import google.auth

    creds = None

    # Load existing token if present
    if TOKEN_PATH.exists():
        with TOKEN_PATH.open("rb") as token_file:
            creds = pickle.load(token_file)

    # If no valid creds, do the OAuth dance
    if not creds or not creds.valid:
        if creds and creds.expired and creds.refresh_token:
            try:
                creds.refresh(Request())
            except google.auth.exceptions.RefreshError:
                creds = None

        if not creds:
            if not CLIENT_SECRET_PATH.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"client_secret_youtube.json not found at {CLIENT_SECRET_PATH}.\n"
                    "Download the OAuth client JSON from Google Cloud and save it there."
                )
            flow = InstalledAppFlow.from_client_secrets_file(
                str(CLIENT_SECRET_PATH),
                SCOPES,
            )
            creds = flow.run_local_server(port=0)

        # Save the token for next time
        with TOKEN_PATH.open("wb") as token_file:
            pickle.dump(creds, token_file)

    return build("youtube", "v3", credentials=creds)


def upload_video(youtube, video_path: Path, title: str, description: str) -> str:
    """
    Upload the given video to YouTube.

    Returns:
        The video ID (string).
    """
    body = {
        "snippet": {
            "title": title,
            "description": description,
            "categoryId": "27",  # Education
        },
        "status": {
            "privacyStatus": "unlisted",  # change to 'public' when you're ready
            "selfDeclaredMadeForKids": False,
        },
    }

    media = MediaFileUpload(
        str(video_path),
        mimetype="video/mp4",
        chunksize=-1,
        resumable=True,
    )

    request = youtube.videos().insert(
        part="snippet,status",
        body=body,
        media_body=media,
    )

    print(f"Uploading {video_path.name} to YouTube...")
    response = None
    while response is None:
        status, response = request.next_chunk()
        if status:
            print(f"Upload progress: {int(status.progress() * 100)}%")

    if "id" not in response:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected response from YouTube API: {response}")

    video_id = response["id"]
    print(f"Upload complete! Video ID: {video_id}")
    return video_id


def main():
    print("=== YouTube Uploader ===")

    video_path = find_latest_video()
    if not video_path:
        print("ERROR: No .mp4 files found in 07_VIDEO.")
        return

    meta_path = find_latest_meta()
    if not meta_path:
        print("ERROR: No *_YOUTUBE_*.txt metadata file found in 07_VIDEO.")
        return

    print(f"Latest video: {video_path.name}")
    print(f"Using metadata: {meta_path.name}")

    title, description, meta_video_name = parse_meta_file(meta_path)

    if meta_video_name and meta_video_name != video_path.name:
        print(
            "WARNING: Metadata 'Video file' does not match latest .mp4 name.\n"
            f"  Meta file says: {meta_video_name}\n"
            f"  Latest video is: {video_path.name}\n"
            "Proceeding with latest video anyway..."
        )

    try:
        youtube = get_authenticated_service()
    except Exception as e:
        print("ERROR: Failed to authenticate with YouTube API:")
        print(e)
        return

    try:
        video_id = upload_video(youtube, video_path, title, description)
    except HttpError as e:
        print("YouTube API error:")
        print(e)
        return

    url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}"
    print(f"\nYouTube URL: {url}\n")
    print("=== Done ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

That’s the whole uploader.

## Next refinement: don’t spam the same b-roll

Right now the system can reuse the same clips a lot. That won’t get you banned (everyone reuses stock), but:

- It can *look* lazy or botted.
- It might hurt watch-time if viewers notice “same visuals, different title”.

The cleanest fix is what you suggested: **track how often we’ve used each clip, and prefer the least-used ones.**

### 1. Upgrade the manifest format

In `06_ASSETS/broll_manifest.json`, each clip entry should look like:

```json
"BROLL/pixabay_6456_city-lights-driving_1.mp4": {
  "usage_count": 0,
  "tags": ["traffic", "lights", "city", "city lights driving"]
}
```

So:

- change existing `"used": true/false` → `"usage_count": 0` (or 1,2,… if already used)
- keep `"tags": [...]` as-is

You don’t have to hand-edit everything; we’ll make the scripts robust so if `usage_count` is missing they treat it as 0.

---

### 2. Tweak `fetch_broll.py` (when adding new clips)

Anywhere it creates a new manifest entry, change from:

```python
clips[rel_key] = {
    "used": False,
    "tags": tags,
}
```

to:

```python
clips[rel_key] = {
    "usage_count": 0,
    "tags": tags,
}
```

That means every freshly downloaded clip starts with **0 uses**.

---

### 3. Change `generate_video_broll.py` to balance usage

Right now it’s thinking in terms of “unused vs used.”  
We want:

- **No more “used” flag**
- Always eligible, but sorted by how often we’ve used them

Here’s the core logic you can change (conceptually):

1. When you build the `all_clips` list, pull `usage_count`:

```python
usage = meta.get("usage_count", 0)
all_clips.append({
    "id": rel,
    "path": clip_path,
    "usage_count": usage,
})
```

2. When picking segments, **sort by usage_count** before shuffling:

```python
# sort by usage_count, then shuffle inside equal buckets so it’s not deterministic
all_clips.sort(key=lambda c: c["usage_count"])
```

3. In `pick_clips_for_segments`, instead of only using “unused entries”, loop through `all_clips` in that sorted order, and after you decide to use one for this video, **increment usage_count**:

```python
clips_meta = manifest.get("clips", {})
selected_segments = []
total = 0.0

for clip in all_clips:
    if total >= audio_duration:
        break

    d = get_duration(clip["path"])
    if d < MIN_CLIP_SECONDS:
        continue

    seg_d = min(d, MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS, audio_duration - total)
    if seg_d <= 0:
        continue

    selected_segments.append((clip["path"], seg_d))
    total += seg_d

    # bump usage_count in manifest
    rel_id = clip["id"]
    entry = clips_meta.get(rel_id, {})
    entry["usage_count"] = entry.get("usage_count", 0) + 1
    clips_meta[rel_id] = entry

if total < audio_duration:
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Not enough b-roll to cover audio with {MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS:.1f}s "
        f"segments per clip. Audio length = {audio_duration:.2f}s, "
        f"b-roll total = {total:.2f}s. Maybe run fetch_broll.py."
    )

manifest["clips"] = clips_meta
return selected_segments, manifest
```

That gives you:

- **Per-video**: each clip appears at most once (we already only cut one segment per clip).
- **Across videos**: clips with low `usage_count` get used first; heavily used clips get pushed to the back.

Over time, as `usage_count` levels out, you’ll get a rotating “pool” instead of a handful of repeats.

## Assistant

Ohhh nice, this is exactly the shape I was hoping your b-roll DB would end up in. ❤️ One big `clips` dict keyed by filename with `tags` + `usage_count` is perfect.

Let me give you something *immediately useful* you can drop into your pipeline: a little “auto-tag + health-check” pass that:

1. **Backfills tags** for anything with `[]` based on the filename pattern (`factory-night`, `blue-collar-work`, etc).
2. **Normalizes some tags** (e.g. ensure a standard tag like `"factory night"` or `"workers"`).
3. **Surfaces what’s unused vs overused** so your selector can bias correctly later.

---

### 1. Recommended tag conventions

Given your filenames, I’d standardize around a small core tag set:

- `factory-night` → `["factory", "night", "industry"]`
- `blue-collar-work` → `["workers", "factory", "labor"]`
- `city-lights-driving` → `["city", "night", "driving"]`
- `rural-road-at-night` → `["rural", "night", "road"]`
- `church-interior` → `["church", "faith", "interior"]`
- `storm-clouds` → `["storm", "clouds", "weather"]`
- `lonely-highway` → `["highway", "road", "night"]`
- `small-town-street` → `["small town", "street", "rural"]`
- `welding-sparks` → `["welding", "sparks", "industry"]`
- `workers-in-rain` → `["workers", "rain", "struggle"]`
- `hands-praying-in-church` → `["hands", "prayer", "church"]`
- `rural-church-at-sunrise` → `["church", "rural", "sunrise"]`
- `old-machinery-closeup` → `["machinery", "closeup", "industrial"]`
- `night-shift-workers` → `["workers", "night shift", "factory"]`

That gives your script something structured to grab even when tags are empty.

---

### 2. Python script to auto-tag + report

Save this as something like `tools/update_broll_tags.py`:

```python
import json
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

BROLL_DB_PATH = Path("broll_db.json")  # <-- change to your actual path


# 1) map filename "themes" to default tags
THEME_TAGS = {
    "factory-night":      ["factory", "night", "industry"],
    "blue-collar-work":   ["workers", "factory", "labor"],
    "city-lights-driving":["city", "night", "driving"],
    "rural-road-at-night":["rural", "night", "road"],
    "church-interior":    ["church", "faith", "interior"],
    "storm-clouds":       ["storm", "clouds", "weather"],
    "lonely-highway":     ["highway", "road", "night"],
    "small-town-street":  ["small town", "street", "rural"],
    "welding-sparks":     ["welding", "sparks", "industry"],
    "workers-in-rain":    ["workers", "rain", "struggle"],
    "hands-praying-in-church": ["hands", "prayer", "church"],
    "rural-church-at-sunrise": ["church", "rural", "sunrise"],
    "old-machinery-closeup": ["machinery", "closeup", "industrial"],
    "night-shift-workers": ["workers", "night shift", "factory"],
}

def infer_theme_from_name(name: str) -> str | None:
    """Find theme key like 'factory-night' inside filename."""
    for theme in THEME_TAGS.keys():
        if theme in name:
            return theme
    return None

def load_db(path: Path) -> dict:
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)

def save_db(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

def auto_tag_and_report():
    db = load_db(BROLL_DB_PATH)
    clips = db.get("clips", {})

    added_tag_count = 0
    untouched = 0
    usage_counter = Counter()

    for clip_name, info in clips.items():
        tags = info.get("tags", [])
        usage = info.get("usage_count", 0)
        usage_counter[clip_name] = usage

        # If tags already exist, skip auto-tagging
        if tags:
            untouched += 1
            continue

        theme = infer_theme_from_name(clip_name)
        if theme:
            default_tags = THEME_TAGS[theme]
            info["tags"] = default_tags
            added_tag_count += len(default_tags)
        else:
            # leave as [], but could optionally add ["uncategorized"]
            pass

    # Save updated DB
    db["clips"] = clips
    save_db(BROLL_DB_PATH, db)

    # Reporting
    total_clips = len(clips)
    zero_use = [name for name, u in usage_counter.items() if u == 0]
    heavy_use = [name for name, u in usage_counter.items() if u >= 3]  # tune threshold

    print(f"Total clips: {total_clips}")
    print(f"Clips with existing tags left untouched: {untouched}")
    print(f"Total tags auto-added: {added_tag_count}")
    print(f"Clips never used (usage_count=0): {len(zero_use)}")
    print(f"Clips heavily used (usage_count>=3): {len(heavy_use)}")

    # Optionally: print a small sample
    print("\nSample never-used clip names:")
    for name in zero_use[:10]:
        print("  -", name)

    print("\nSample heavy-used clip names:")
    for name in heavy_use[:10]:
        print("  -", name)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    auto_tag_and_report()
```

## 2. Make a tolerant loader/saver

Since we don’t know the exact structure of `broll_manifest.json` yet, let’s write a loader that:

- If it already has `{"clips": { ... }}`, it uses that directly.  
- If it’s a **list** of clip paths, or a **dict** keyed by path without `usage_count`, it wraps/initializes into our canonical shape.

Add this:

```python
def _normalize_broll_db(raw) -> dict:
    """
    Convert whatever is in broll_manifest.json into:

    {
      "clips": {
        "path/to/file.mp4": {
          "tags": [...],
          "usage_count": int
        },
        ...
      }
    }
    """
    # Case 1: already in canonical form
    if isinstance(raw, dict) and "clips" in raw:
        clips = raw["clips"]
    else:
        clips = {}

        # Case 2: list of paths
        if isinstance(raw, list):
            for path in raw:
                clips[str(path)] = {"tags": [], "usage_count": 0}

        # Case 3: dict keyed by path
        elif isinstance(raw, dict):
            for path, meta in raw.items():
                if isinstance(meta, dict):
                    tags = meta.get("tags", [])
                    usage = meta.get("usage_count", 0)
                else:
                    tags = []
                    usage = 0
                clips[str(path)] = {"tags": tags, "usage_count": usage}

        # Anything else -> empty
    return {"clips": clips}


def load_broll_db() -> dict:
    if os.path.exists(BROLL_DB_PATH):
        with open(BROLL_DB_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            raw = json.load(f)
        return _normalize_broll_db(raw)

    # Fresh DB if the file doesn't exist yet
    return {"clips": {}}


def save_broll_db(db: dict) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(BROLL_DB_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    with open(BROLL_DB_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(db, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
```

"""
generate_video_broll.py

Builds a video by stitching together stock b-roll clips from
06_ASSETS/BROLL and overlaying the latest audio from 05_AUDIO.

Usage model:
- Each individual clip file can be reused across different videos.
- Within a SINGLE video, we never use the same clip twice.
- We track per-clip `usage_count` in 06_ASSETS/broll_manifest.json.
- When building a new video, we prefer clips with LOWER usage_count.

Pacing:
- We take short segments (up to MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS) from each clip.
- Each segment is normalized to:
    - 1920x1080
    - 30fps
    - yuv420p
- Then we concatenate those segments.
- Finally, we mux the montage with the latest narration audio.

Run from MC_Factory root:

    (.mc_env) python 04_SCRIPTS/generate_video_broll.py
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Tuple
import os
import json

# Base dir = MC_Factory
BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__))

# Use your existing manifest as the DB
BROLL_DB_PATH = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "06_ASSETS", "broll_manifest.json")


# ---- Config ----

FFMPEG_BIN_DIR = Path(r"C:\ffmpeg\bin")
FFMPEG_EXE = FFMPEG_BIN_DIR / "ffmpeg.exe"
FFPROBE_EXE = FFMPEG_BIN_DIR / "ffprobe.exe"

SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BASE_DIR = SCRIPT_DIR.parent  # MC_Factory

AUDIO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "05_AUDIO"
ASSETS_DIR = BASE_DIR / "06_ASSETS"
BROLL_DIR = ASSETS_DIR / "BROLL"
VIDEO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "07_VIDEO"
MANIFEST_PATH = ASSETS_DIR / "broll_manifest.json"

MIN_CLIP_SECONDS = 1.0
MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS = 8.0


# ---- Subprocess helpers ----

def run_cmd(args: List[str]) -> str:
    """Run a subprocess and return stdout as text, or raise on error."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        args,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print("Command failed:", " ".join(args))
        print("STDERR:", result.stderr)
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed with code {result.returncode}")
    return result.stdout


def get_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    """Return duration in seconds using ffprobe."""
    cmd = [
        str(FFPROBE_EXE),
        "-v", "error",
        "-show_entries", "format=duration",
        "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1",
        str(path),
    ]
    out = run_cmd(cmd).strip()
    try:
        return float(out)
    except ValueError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not parse duration for {path}: {out!r}")


# ---- Manifest helpers ----

def load_manifest() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Load broll_manifest.json and migrate any old 'used' flags to 'usage_count'.
    Structure:

    {
      "clips": {
        "BROLL/foo.mp4": {
          "usage_count": int,
          "tags": [...]
        },
        ...
      }
    }
    """
    if MANIFEST_PATH.exists():
        with MANIFEST_PATH.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            manifest = json.load(f)
    else:
        manifest = {"clips": {}}

    clips = manifest.get("clips", {})
    changed = False

    for rel, meta in list(clips.items()):
        if not isinstance(meta, dict):
            clips[rel] = {"usage_count": 0, "tags": []}
            changed = True
            continue

        # Migrate old 'used' flag to 'usage_count' if necessary
        if "usage_count" not in meta:
            used_flag = meta.get("used", False)
            usage = 1 if used_flag else 0
            meta["usage_count"] = usage
            changed = True

        # Ensure tags exists
        if "tags" not in meta or not isinstance(meta["tags"], list):
            meta["tags"] = []
            changed = True

        # Clean up old fields
        if "used" in meta:
            del meta["used"]
            changed = True

        clips[rel] = meta

    manifest["clips"] = clips

    if changed:
        with MANIFEST_PATH.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(manifest, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

    return manifest


def save_manifest(manifest: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    MANIFEST_PATH.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with MANIFEST_PATH.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)


def sync_manifest_with_fs(manifest: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Align manifest with actual files on disk:
    - Add any .mp4 in 06_ASSETS/BROLL not in manifest.
    - Remove any manifest entry whose file no longer exists.
    """
    clips = manifest.get("clips", {})

    fs_paths: List[str] = []
    if BROLL_DIR.exists():
        for p in BROLL_DIR.iterdir():
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".mp4":
                rel = p.relative_to(ASSETS_DIR).as_posix()  # e.g. "BROLL/foo.mp4"
                fs_paths.append(rel)

    fs_set = set(fs_paths)

    # Add new clips
    for rel in fs_paths:
        if rel not in clips:
            clips[rel] = {
                "usage_count": 0,
                "tags": [],
            }

    # Remove missing clips
    for rel in list(clips.keys()):
        if rel not in fs_set:
            del clips[rel]

    manifest["clips"] = clips
    return manifest


# ---- Audio helpers ----

def find_latest_audio() -> Path | None:
    if not AUDIO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    audio_files = sorted(
        [
            p for p in AUDIO_DIR.iterdir()
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in {".mp3", ".wav"}
        ],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return audio_files[0] if audio_files else None


# ---- Clip selection ----

def pick_segments_for_audio(
    manifest: Dict[str, Any],
    audio_duration: float
) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[Path, float]], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Choose clips to cover the audio duration.

    - We only take up to MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS from each clip.
    - We never use the same clip twice in a single video.
    - After selection, we increment usage_count for each chosen clip.

    Returns:
        ([(clip_path, seg_duration), ...], updated_manifest)

    If there is not enough total footage to cover the audio, we raise RuntimeError.
    """
    clips_meta = manifest.get("clips", {})
    if not clips_meta:
        raise RuntimeError("No clips in manifest. Run fetch_broll.py first.")

    # Build list of available clips with abs paths
    clip_entries = []
    for rel, meta in clips_meta.items():
        abs_path = ASSETS_DIR / rel
        if abs_path.is_file():
            usage_count = int(meta.get("usage_count", 0))
            clip_entries.append({
                "rel": rel,
                "path": abs_path,
                "usage_count": usage_count,
            })

    if not clip_entries:
        raise RuntimeError("No valid clip files found on disk. Run fetch_broll.py.")

    # Shuffle for randomness, then sort by usage_count so we prefer underused clips
    random.shuffle(clip_entries)
    clip_entries.sort(key=lambda c: c["usage_count"])

    selected_segments: List[Tuple[Path, float]] = []
    total_seg_duration = 0.0
    used_this_video: List[str] = []  # rel paths used in THIS video

    for entry in clip_entries:
        if total_seg_duration >= audio_duration:
            break

        rel = entry["rel"]
        path = entry["path"]

        if rel in used_this_video:
            continue

        d = get_duration(path)
        if d < MIN_CLIP_SECONDS:
            print(f"Skipping very short clip ({d:.2f}s): {path.name}")
            continue

        remaining = audio_duration - total_seg_duration
        seg_duration = min(d, MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS, remaining)
        if seg_duration <= 0:
            continue

        selected_segments.append((path, seg_duration))
        total_seg_duration += seg_duration
        used_this_video.append(rel)

        # If we've used every clip once and still haven't covered audio, we stop
        if len(used_this_video) == len(clip_entries):
            break

    if total_seg_duration < audio_duration:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Not enough total b-roll to cover audio with {MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS:.1f}s "
            f"segments per clip. Audio length = {audio_duration:.2f}s, "
            f"b-roll total = {total_seg_duration:.2f}s. "
            "Run fetch_broll.py to add more clips."
        )

    # Increment usage_count for all clips used in this video
    for rel in used_this_video:
        if rel in clips_meta:
            clips_meta[rel]["usage_count"] = int(clips_meta[rel].get("usage_count", 0)) + 1

    manifest["clips"] = clips_meta
    return selected_segments, manifest


# ---- Main ----

def main():
    print("=== Generating B-roll Video (short segments, balanced reuse) ===")

    # Check ffmpeg/ffprobe
    if not FFMPEG_EXE.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: ffmpeg not found at {FFMPEG_EXE}")
        sys.exit(1)
    if not FFPROBE_EXE.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: ffprobe not found at {FFPROBE_EXE}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Find latest audio
    audio_path = find_latest_audio()
    if not audio_path:
        print("ERROR: No audio files found in 05_AUDIO.")
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"Using audio: {audio_path.name}")
    audio_duration = get_duration(audio_path)
    print(f"Audio duration: {audio_duration:.2f} seconds")

    # Load + sync manifest
    manifest = load_manifest()
    manifest = sync_manifest_with_fs(manifest)

    # Pick clips & segment durations
    try:
        segments, manifest = pick_segments_for_audio(manifest, audio_duration)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print("ERROR:", e)
        save_manifest(manifest)  # keep any sync changes
        sys.exit(1)

    # Persist updated usage_count
    save_manifest(manifest)

    print(f"\nSelected {len(segments)} clips for segments (max {MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS:.1f}s each):")
    total_seg = 0.0
    for clip_path, seg_d in segments:
        total_seg += seg_d
        print(f" - {clip_path.name}: segment {seg_d:.2f}s")
    print(f"Total planned segment duration: {total_seg:.2f} seconds")

    VIDEO_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    # Create a temp subdir for segments
    temp_dir = VIDEO_DIR / "temp_segments"
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    # For concat list
    temp_concat_list = VIDEO_DIR / "broll_concat_list.txt"
    segment_files: List[Path] = []

    print("\n=== Creating normalized segments ===")
    for idx, (clip_path, seg_d) in enumerate(segments):
        seg_out = temp_dir / f"seg_{idx:03d}.mp4"
        print(f"Segment {idx+1}/{len(segments)}: {clip_path.name} -> {seg_out.name} ({seg_d:.2f}s)")
        segment_files.append(seg_out)

        cmd = [
            str(FFMPEG_EXE),
            "-y",
            "-i", str(clip_path),
            "-t", f"{seg_d:.3f}",
            "-vf",
            (
                "scale=1920:1080:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"
                "setsar=1,"
                "pad=1920:1080:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,"
                "format=yuv420p"
            ),
            "-r", "30",
            "-c:v", "libx264",
            "-preset", "fast",
            "-crf", "20",
            "-an",  # strip any audio from the b-roll segment
            str(seg_out),
        ]
        run_cmd(cmd)

    # Write concat list
    with temp_concat_list.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for seg in segment_files:
            f.write(f"file '{seg.as_posix()}'\n")

    temp_video = VIDEO_DIR / "broll_temp.mp4"

    print("\n=== Concatenating segments ===")
    concat_cmd = [
        str(FFMPEG_EXE),
        "-y",
        "-f", "concat",
        "-safe", "0",
        "-i", str(temp_concat_list),
        "-c:v", "copy",
        str(temp_video),
    ]
    run_cmd(concat_cmd)
    print(f"Temp concatenated video: {temp_video}")

    # Final mux with audio
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    base_name = audio_path.stem
    out_path = VIDEO_DIR / f"{base_name}_broll_{timestamp}.mp4"

    print("\n=== Muxing audio + concatenated video ===")
    mux_cmd = [
        str(FFMPEG_EXE),
        "-y",
        "-i", str(temp_video),   # 0 = b-roll video only
        "-i", str(audio_path),   # 1 = narration audio
        "-map", "0:v:0",
        "-map", "1:a:0",
        "-c:v", "copy",
        "-c:a", "aac",
        "-shortest",
        str(out_path),
    ]
    run_cmd(mux_cmd)

    print(f"\nSaved final video to: {out_path}")
    print("=== Done ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```json
{
  "clips": {
    "BROLL/5542449-hd_1920_1080_30fps.mp4": {
      "usage_count": 3,
      "tags": ["construction", "wide"]
    },
    "BROLL/5875508-uhd_3840_2160_24fps.mp4": {
      "usage_count": 0,
      "tags": []
    }
  }
}
```

Key details:

- Top-level `"clips"` object.
- Keys inside `"clips"` are **relative paths from `06_ASSETS`**, e.g. `"BROLL/foo.mp4"`.
- Each entry has:
  - `usage_count` (int, how many times we’ve used this clip across all videos)
  - `tags` (list, currently unused but ready for “talking head”, “factory floor”, etc.)

### Auto-migration

`load_manifest()` will try to **migrate** older formats:

```python
if MANIFEST_PATH.exists():
    manifest = json.load(...)
else:
    manifest = {"clips": {}}
```

Then it walks each clip entry:

- If meta is not a dict → replaces it with `{"usage_count": 0, "tags": []}`
- If it finds a legacy `"used": true/false` flag, it converts that into:
  - `usage_count = 1` if used
  - `usage_count = 0` if not
- Ensures `tags` exists as a list
- Deletes the old `"used"` key

So as long as your JSON is *somewhat* sane, this function will normalize it into the new structure.

---

## 3. How clip selection + usage tracking works

The key function is `pick_segments_for_audio(...)`:

1. It builds a list of all `.mp4` files present under `06_ASSETS/BROLL`.
2. It pairs them with their `usage_count` from the manifest.
3. It shuffles for randomness, then sorts so **lowest `usage_count` comes first**:

   ```python
   random.shuffle(clip_entries)
   clip_entries.sort(key=lambda c: c["usage_count"])
   ```

4. It walks that list, one clip per segment, never repeating a clip within the same video:

   ```python
   used_this_video: List[str] = []
   ...
   if rel in used_this_video:
       continue
   ```

5. For each chosen clip it:
   - Computes its duration with `ffprobe`
   - Chooses a segment length `seg_duration` up to `MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS` (8s) or whatever’s left in the audio.
   - Adds `(clip_path, seg_duration)` to the plan.

6. When done, it increments usage counts for all clips used in this run:

   ```python
   for rel in used_this_video:
       clips_meta[rel]["usage_count"] = int(clips_meta[rel].get("usage_count", 0)) + 1
   ```

7. Then `save_manifest(manifest)` writes the updated JSON back out to `06_ASSETS/broll_manifest.json`.

So behavior right now is:

- **Within a single video**: no clip is used twice.
- **Across multiple videos**: all clips can be reused, but clips that have been used fewer times are **strongly favored**.

That’s exactly what your top-of-file docstring says you wanted.

## Target behavior (what the system should eventually do)

For *one* script:

1. **Ingest the script**
   - Input: `script_XYZ.txt` or a transcript.
   - Break it into time-chunks (e.g. one chunk per sentence or 5–10s blocks).

2. **Auto-tag each chunk**
   - For each chunk, generate tags like:
     - `"factory"`, `"office"`, `"workers"`, `"graphs"`, `"city skyline"`, `"coding"`, etc.
   - You end up with something like:

     ```json
     [
       {"start": 0.0,  "end": 8.5,  "tags": ["factory", "robots", "industry"]},
       {"start": 8.5,  "end": 17.0, "tags": ["office", "laptop", "charts"]},
       ...
     ]
     ```

3. **For each chunk, pick b-roll**
   For each chunk’s tag set:

   - Look in your **b-roll DB** for clips whose tags overlap.
   - Score each candidate clip using:
     - **Topical match** (how many tags overlap).
     - **Usage_count penalty** (clips that have been used a lot get penalized).
     - **Recent usage penalty** (prefer not to repeat something used in the *last* few videos).
   - If **no candidate** scores high enough:
     - Call the downloader (Pexels, Pixabay, Storyblocks, etc.) for that tag set.
     - Download new clips, add them to the DB with tags + usage_count=0.

4. **Make a segment plan**
   - For each chunk, choose one clip and a segment duration that roughly fits the chunk length.
   - Don’t reuse the exact same clip twice in the *same* video unless you absolutely must.
   - Across videos, reuse is allowed but controlled by the scoring.

5. **Update the DB**
   - After the video is built, increment `usage_count` for every clip that was used.
   - Log that this clip appeared in `video_XYZ` on `2025-11-30` (so you can avoid over-repetition in a short time window).

6. **Render like you already do**
   - Take the segment plan, run ffmpeg exactly as `generate_video_broll.py` is doing now.
   - Mux with audio, etc.

## What we need to support that: DB shape

Right now your manifest is **per-clip, flat**, with:

```json
{
  "clips": {
    "BROLL/foo.mp4": {
      "usage_count": 3,
      "tags": []
    }
  }
}
```

To reach your goal, the *same file* can still be the “database,” but its **schema needs to grow** a bit.

Think something like:

```json
{
  "clips": {
    "BROLL/factory_robots_01.mp4": {
      "usage_count": 3,
      "tags": ["factory", "robots", "industry", "conveyor"],
      "source": {
        "provider": "pexels",
        "id": "1234567"
      },
      "added_at": "2025-11-30T18:12:00",
      "last_used_at": "2025-11-30T19:05:10",
      "videos_used_in": [
        "script_mc-001-long_20251116_061746",
        "script_mc-002-short_20251120_073210"
      ]
    }
  },
  "videos": {
    "script_mc-001-long_20251116_061746": {
      "created_at": "2025-11-16T06:17:46",
      "script_path": "03_SCRIPTS/script_mc-001-long.txt",
      "segments": [
        {
          "start": 0.0,
          "end": 7.8,
          "clip": "BROLL/factory_robots_01.mp4"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

You don’t *have* to add the `videos` section yet, but this is the sort of thing that makes “algorithm-aware” reuse possible.

## How auto-tagging & download fit into your current script

Right now `generate_video_broll.py` does:

- Load `broll_manifest.json`
- Sync with local `BROLL/`
- Pick random-ish clips biased by low `usage_count`
- Render

In the **future** world, the flow becomes:

1. **script → chunk tags**  
   New script: e.g. `plan_broll_from_script.py` that outputs a JSON file with time-chunks and tags.

2. **chunk tags → clip selection**  
   New function (or script) that:
   - Reads the chunk-tags JSON.
   - Talks to the manifest to find best matches.
   - Optionally calls the downloader to expand the library when needed.
   - Outputs a **segment plan JSON**, e.g.:

     ```json
     [
       {
         "clip": "BROLL/factory_robots_01.mp4",
         "segment_start": 12.3,
         "segment_duration": 7.5
       },
       {
         "clip": "BROLL/office_team_meeting_02.mp4",
         "segment_start": 0.0,
         "segment_duration": 6.9
       }
     ]
     ```

3. **segment plan → final video**  
   `generate_video_broll.py` morphs into something like `render_broll_video.py`:
   - It *only* cares about:
     - Which file
     - Start time
     - Segment duration
   - No more “figure out which clips”—that’s done upstream.

We don’t have to do all that at once. We can grow into it.

## Assistant

Perfect, this manifest is exactly what we need to start getting “smart” instead of random.

Given what you want:

> take a script → auto-tag it → compare against existing clips → decide reuse vs new download → pick clips in an algorithm-aware way

I’ll give you a *concrete implementation plan* and then actual Python code you can drop in.

---

## 1. What we’ll add conceptually

We’ll bolt three brains onto your current pipeline:

1. **Script → tags**  
   Look at the script text and decide what *visual themes* it needs, e.g.
   - “factory”, “night”, “industry” → `{"factory-night"}`
   - “workers”, “job site”, “blue collar” → `{"blue-collar-work"}`
   - “church”, “faith”, “God” → `{"church-interior", "hands-praying-in-church", "rural-church-at-sunrise"}`
   - “storm”, “crash”, “risk” → `{"storm-clouds"}`
   - “driving home, highway, commute” → `{"rural-road-at-night", "city-lights-driving", "lonely-highway"}`

2. **Manifest → fast lookup**
   Use your existing `broll_manifest.json` to pick clips that:
   - have **overlapping tags** with the script needs
   - have **low usage_count** (favor under-used clips)
   - avoid reusing the same clip too many times in the same video

3. **Reuse vs new download policy**
   For each high-level tag:
   - If there are enough **good existing clips** (e.g. ≥ 10 with low usage_count), reuse.
   - If not, call a `download_new_broll(tag)` helper that:
     - Downloads new clips for that tag
     - Adds them to `BROLL/`
     - Updates `broll_manifest.json`

The “algorithm-aware decisions” can be encoded as simple weights:
- Score = `tag_overlap_score – α * usage_count – β * recently_used_penalty`
- Then pick the highest-score clip for each segment.

---

## 2. New helper module: `broll_selector.py`

Create `broll_selector.py` next to `generate_video_broll.py` with something like this:

```python
# broll_selector.py

import json
import os
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Dict, List, Set, Tuple

MANIFEST_PATH = "broll_manifest.json"


ClipInfo = Dict[str, object]  # path -> {"tags": [..], "usage_count": int}


# ---------- Manifest load/save ----------

def load_manifest(path: str = MANIFEST_PATH) -> Dict[str, ClipInfo]:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return {"clips": {}}
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


def save_manifest(manifest: Dict[str, ClipInfo], path: str = MANIFEST_PATH) -> None:
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)


# ---------- Script → high-level visual tags ----------

def extract_script_tags(script_text: str) -> Set[str]:
    """
    Very dumb but effective keyword matcher.
    You can refine this later, but this gives you
    a first pass of 'visual themes' to look for.
    """
    text = script_text.lower()

    tag_groups = {
        "factory-night": [
            "factory", "plant", "industrial", "industry", "smokestack", "refinery"
        ],
        "blue-collar-work": [
            "worker", "job site", "hard hat", "blue collar", "construction", "welding"
        ],
        "church-interior": [
            "church", "cathedral", "pew", "altar", "sanctuary"
        ],
        "hands-praying-in-church": [
            "prayer", "praying", "hands together", "faith", "god", "jesus"
        ],
        "rural-church-at-sunrise": [
            "sunrise", "sunset", "morning light", "field", "pasture", "farm", "country"
        ],
        "storm-clouds": [
            "storm", "crash", "collapse", "risk", "crisis", "volatility", "tornado",
            "hurricane", "thunderstorm", "lightning"
        ],
        "city-lights-driving": [
            "city", "night drive", "commute", "traffic", "downtown", "urban"
        ],
        "rural-road-at-night": [
            "lonely road", "back road", "backroad", "country road", "dark road",
            "two lane", "driving home", "night highway"
        ],
        "lonely-highway": [
            "interstate", "highway", "long drive", "on the road"
        ],
        "welding-sparks": [
            "sparks", "welding", "grinding", "metalwork", "steel"
        ],
        "workers-in-rain": [
            "rain", "stormy day", "bad weather", "soaking", "wet on the job"
        ],
        "old-machinery-closeup": [
            "machine", "gears", "rusty", "old equipment", "mechanism"
        ],
        "night-shift-workers": [
            "night shift", "graveyard shift", "3rd shift", "late shift"
        ],
    }

    selected: Set[str] = set()
    for tag, keywords in tag_groups.items():
        if any(kw in text for kw in keywords):
            selected.add(tag)

    # Always have at least some generic fallback
    if not selected:
        selected.add("city-lights-driving")

    return selected


# ---------- Manifest indexing ----------

def index_clips_by_tag(manifest: Dict[str, ClipInfo]) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
    """
    Build a reverse index: tag -> [clip_paths...]
    Uses both the pixabay-style tags and the 'coarse' theme encoded
    at the end of the filename (e.g. *_factory-night_1.mp4).
    """
    clips = manifest.get("clips", {})
    index: Dict[str, List[str]] = defaultdict(list)

    for path, info in clips.items():
        tags: List[str] = info.get("tags", []) or []
        tags_lower = {t.lower() for t in tags}

        # coarse tag from filename suffix, e.g. ..._factory-night_1.mp4
        base = os.path.basename(path)
        parts = base.split("_")
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            coarse = parts[-2].lower()  # 'factory-night', 'rural-road-at-night', etc.
            tags_lower.add(coarse)

        for t in tags_lower:
            index[t].append(path)

    return index


# ---------- Scoring & selection ----------

def score_clip(
    clip_tags: Set[str],
    desired_tags: Set[str],
    usage_count: int,
    recently_used: Set[str],
    path: str,
) -> float:
    """
    Higher is better.
    - More tag overlap increases score.
    - Higher usage_count decreases score.
    - If recently used in this same video, big penalty.
    """
    overlap = len(clip_tags & desired_tags)
    if overlap == 0:
        return -1e9  # don't use at all

    base = float(overlap)

    # Penalize heavy reuse a bit
    base -= 0.1 * usage_count

    # Extra penalty if we've already used this clip in the current video
    if path in recently_used:
        base -= 2.0

    return base


def choose_clip_for_segment(
    segment_text: str,
    manifest: Dict[str, ClipInfo],
    desired_tags: Set[str],
    recently_used: Set[str],
) -> str | None:
    """
    Pick the best clip path for this segment, or None if nothing fits.
    """
    clips = manifest.get("clips", {})
    if not clips:
        return None

    segment_tags = extract_script_tags(segment_text)  # you can also make this more local
    effective_tags = desired_tags | segment_tags

    best_path = None
    best_score = -1e9

    for path, info in clips.items():
        tags_set = set(t.lower() for t in (info.get("tags") or []))

        # add coarse tag from filename
        base = os.path.basename(path)
        parts = base.split("_")
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            tags_set.add(parts[-2].lower())

        usage_count = int(info.get("usage_count", 0))

        s = score_clip(tags_set, effective_tags, usage_count, recently_used, path)
        if s > best_score:
            best_score = s
            best_path = path

    if best_score < -1e8:
        return None

    return best_path


def bump_usage_counts(manifest: Dict[str, ClipInfo], chosen_paths: List[str]) -> None:
    for path in chosen_paths:
        info = manifest["clips"].setdefault(path, {"tags": [], "usage_count": 0})
        info["usage_count"] = int(info.get("usage_count", 0)) + 1


# ---------- (Optional) Download new b-roll ----------

def download_new_broll_for_tags(
    needed_tags: Set[str],
    manifest: Dict[str, ClipInfo],
) -> None:
    """
    Placeholder: this is where you'd integrate your pixabay/stock API.
    For now it does nothing, but the shape is here so your main script
    can call it when there aren't enough clips for a tag.
    """
    # You could:
    # - call an API
    # - save into BROLL/<something>.mp4
    # - add entries into manifest["clips"][path] = {"tags": [...], "usage_count": 0}
    pass
```

That gives us:

- `extract_script_tags(script_text)` – global tags from the whole script
- `choose_clip_for_segment(segment_text, manifest, desired_tags, recently_used)`
- `bump_usage_counts(manifest, chosen_paths)`

---

## 3. Wire it into `generate_video_broll.py`

In your existing `generate_video_broll.py` (the one that already prints:

> `Selected 29 clips for segments (max 8.0s each): ...`

you’ll change the part that currently picks clips randomly.

Roughly, the flow becomes:

```python
# generate_video_broll.py  (only the important parts)

from pathlib import Path
import json

from broll_selector import (
    load_manifest,
    save_manifest,
    extract_script_tags,
    choose_clip_for_segment,
    bump_usage_counts,
    download_new_broll_for_tags,
)


def generate_broll_for_script(script_text: str, segment_texts: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    manifest = load_manifest()
    desired_tags = extract_script_tags(script_text)

    # Optional: check if we have enough clips per tag, otherwise download more
    download_new_broll_for_tags(desired_tags, manifest)

    chosen_paths: list[str] = []
    recently_used: set[str] = set()

    for seg in segment_texts:
        clip = choose_clip_for_segment(
            segment_text=seg,
            manifest=manifest,
            desired_tags=desired_tags,
            recently_used=recently_used,
        )
        if clip is None:
            # fallback: just don't add b-roll for this segment, or pick any low-usage clip
            clip = None

        if clip:
            chosen_paths.append(clip)
            recently_used.add(clip)

    # Update usage counts and save manifest
    bump_usage_counts(manifest, chosen_paths)
    save_manifest(manifest)

    return chosen_paths
```

Then wherever you *currently* build your list of segments (with timestamps) you would do something like:


generate_video_broll.py currently 

"""
generate_video_broll.py

Builds a video by stitching together stock b-roll clips from
06_ASSETS/BROLL and overlaying the latest audio from 05_AUDIO.

Usage model:
- Each individual clip file can be reused across different videos.
- Within a SINGLE video, we never use the same clip twice.
- We track per-clip `usage_count` in 06_ASSETS/broll_manifest.json.
- When building a new video, we prefer clips with LOWER usage_count.

Pacing:
- We take short segments (up to MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS) from each clip.
- Each segment is normalized to:
    - 1920x1080
    - 30fps
    - yuv420p
- Then we concatenate those segments.
- Finally, we mux the montage with the latest narration audio.

Run from MC_Factory root:

    (.mc_env) python 04_SCRIPTS/generate_video_broll.py
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Tuple
import os
import json

# Base dir = MC_Factory
BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__))

# Use your existing manifest as the DB
BROLL_DB_PATH = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "06_ASSETS", "broll_manifest.json")


# ---- Config ----

FFMPEG_BIN_DIR = Path(r"C:\ffmpeg\bin")
FFMPEG_EXE = FFMPEG_BIN_DIR / "ffmpeg.exe"
FFPROBE_EXE = FFMPEG_BIN_DIR / "ffprobe.exe"

SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BASE_DIR = SCRIPT_DIR.parent  # MC_Factory

AUDIO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "05_AUDIO"
ASSETS_DIR = BASE_DIR / "06_ASSETS"
BROLL_DIR = ASSETS_DIR / "BROLL"
VIDEO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "07_VIDEO"
MANIFEST_PATH = ASSETS_DIR / "broll_manifest.json"

MIN_CLIP_SECONDS = 1.0
MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS = 8.0


# ---- Subprocess helpers ----

def run_cmd(args: List[str]) -> str:
    """Run a subprocess and return stdout as text, or raise on error."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        args,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print("Command failed:", " ".join(args))
        print("STDERR:", result.stderr)
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed with code {result.returncode}")
    return result.stdout


def get_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    """Return duration in seconds using ffprobe."""
    cmd = [
        str(FFPROBE_EXE),
        "-v", "error",
        "-show_entries", "format=duration",
        "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1",
        str(path),
    ]
    out = run_cmd(cmd).strip()
    try:
        return float(out)
    except ValueError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not parse duration for {path}: {out!r}")


# ---- Manifest helpers ----

def load_manifest() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Load broll_manifest.json and migrate any old 'used' flags to 'usage_count'.
    Structure:

    {
      "clips": {
        "BROLL/foo.mp4": {
          "usage_count": int,
          "tags": [...]
        },
        ...
      }
    }
    """
    if MANIFEST_PATH.exists():
        with MANIFEST_PATH.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            manifest = json.load(f)
    else:
        manifest = {"clips": {}}

    clips = manifest.get("clips", {})
    changed = False

    for rel, meta in list(clips.items()):
        if not isinstance(meta, dict):
            clips[rel] = {"usage_count": 0, "tags": []}
            changed = True
            continue

        # Migrate old 'used' flag to 'usage_count' if necessary
        if "usage_count" not in meta:
            used_flag = meta.get("used", False)
            usage = 1 if used_flag else 0
            meta["usage_count"] = usage
            changed = True

        # Ensure tags exists
        if "tags" not in meta or not isinstance(meta["tags"], list):
            meta["tags"] = []
            changed = True

        # Clean up old fields
        if "used" in meta:
            del meta["used"]
            changed = True

        clips[rel] = meta

    manifest["clips"] = clips

    if changed:
        with MANIFEST_PATH.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(manifest, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

    return manifest


def save_manifest(manifest: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    MANIFEST_PATH.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with MANIFEST_PATH.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)


def sync_manifest_with_fs(manifest: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Align manifest with actual files on disk:
    - Add any .mp4 in 06_ASSETS/BROLL not in manifest.
    - Remove any manifest entry whose file no longer exists.
    """
    clips = manifest.get("clips", {})

    fs_paths: List[str] = []
    if BROLL_DIR.exists():
        for p in BROLL_DIR.iterdir():
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".mp4":
                rel = p.relative_to(ASSETS_DIR).as_posix()  # e.g. "BROLL/foo.mp4"
                fs_paths.append(rel)

    fs_set = set(fs_paths)

    # Add new clips
    for rel in fs_paths:
        if rel not in clips:
            clips[rel] = {
                "usage_count": 0,
                "tags": [],
            }

    # Remove missing clips
    for rel in list(clips.keys()):
        if rel not in fs_set:
            del clips[rel]

    manifest["clips"] = clips
    return manifest


# ---- Audio helpers ----

def find_latest_audio() -> Path | None:
    if not AUDIO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    audio_files = sorted(
        [
            p for p in AUDIO_DIR.iterdir()
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in {".mp3", ".wav"}
        ],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return audio_files[0] if audio_files else None


# ---- Clip selection ----

def pick_segments_for_audio(
    manifest: Dict[str, Any],
    audio_duration: float
) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[Path, float]], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Choose clips to cover the audio duration.

    - We only take up to MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS from each clip.
    - We never use the same clip twice in a single video.
    - After selection, we increment usage_count for each chosen clip.

    Returns:
        ([(clip_path, seg_duration), ...], updated_manifest)

    If there is not enough total footage to cover the audio, we raise RuntimeError.
    """
    clips_meta = manifest.get("clips", {})
    if not clips_meta:
        raise RuntimeError("No clips in manifest. Run fetch_broll.py first.")

    # Build list of available clips with abs paths
    clip_entries = []
    for rel, meta in clips_meta.items():
        abs_path = ASSETS_DIR / rel
        if abs_path.is_file():
            usage_count = int(meta.get("usage_count", 0))
            clip_entries.append({
                "rel": rel,
                "path": abs_path,
                "usage_count": usage_count,
            })

    if not clip_entries:
        raise RuntimeError("No valid clip files found on disk. Run fetch_broll.py.")

    # Shuffle for randomness, then sort by usage_count so we prefer underused clips
    random.shuffle(clip_entries)
    clip_entries.sort(key=lambda c: c["usage_count"])

    selected_segments: List[Tuple[Path, float]] = []
    total_seg_duration = 0.0
    used_this_video: List[str] = []  # rel paths used in THIS video

    for entry in clip_entries:
        if total_seg_duration >= audio_duration:
            break

        rel = entry["rel"]
        path = entry["path"]

        if rel in used_this_video:
            continue

        d = get_duration(path)
        if d < MIN_CLIP_SECONDS:
            print(f"Skipping very short clip ({d:.2f}s): {path.name}")
            continue

        remaining = audio_duration - total_seg_duration
        seg_duration = min(d, MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS, remaining)
        if seg_duration <= 0:
            continue

        selected_segments.append((path, seg_duration))
        total_seg_duration += seg_duration
        used_this_video.append(rel)

        # If we've used every clip once and still haven't covered audio, we stop
        if len(used_this_video) == len(clip_entries):
            break

    if total_seg_duration < audio_duration:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Not enough total b-roll to cover audio with {MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS:.1f}s "
            f"segments per clip. Audio length = {audio_duration:.2f}s, "
            f"b-roll total = {total_seg_duration:.2f}s. "
            "Run fetch_broll.py to add more clips."
        )

    # Increment usage_count for all clips used in this video
    for rel in used_this_video:
        if rel in clips_meta:
            clips_meta[rel]["usage_count"] = int(clips_meta[rel].get("usage_count", 0)) + 1

    manifest["clips"] = clips_meta
    return selected_segments, manifest


# ---- Main ----

def main():
    print("=== Generating B-roll Video (short segments, balanced reuse) ===")

    # Check ffmpeg/ffprobe
    if not FFMPEG_EXE.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: ffmpeg not found at {FFMPEG_EXE}")
        sys.exit(1)
    if not FFPROBE_EXE.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: ffprobe not found at {FFPROBE_EXE}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Find latest audio
    audio_path = find_latest_audio()
    if not audio_path:
        print("ERROR: No audio files found in 05_AUDIO.")
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"Using audio: {audio_path.name}")
    audio_duration = get_duration(audio_path)
    print(f"Audio duration: {audio_duration:.2f} seconds")

    # Load + sync manifest
    manifest = load_manifest()
    manifest = sync_manifest_with_fs(manifest)

    # Pick clips & segment durations
    try:
        segments, manifest = pick_segments_for_audio(manifest, audio_duration)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print("ERROR:", e)
        save_manifest(manifest)  # keep any sync changes
        sys.exit(1)

    # Persist updated usage_count
    save_manifest(manifest)

    print(f"\nSelected {len(segments)} clips for segments (max {MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS:.1f}s each):")
    total_seg = 0.0
    for clip_path, seg_d in segments:
        total_seg += seg_d
        print(f" - {clip_path.name}: segment {seg_d:.2f}s")
    print(f"Total planned segment duration: {total_seg:.2f} seconds")

    VIDEO_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    # Create a temp subdir for segments
    temp_dir = VIDEO_DIR / "temp_segments"
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    # For concat list
    temp_concat_list = VIDEO_DIR / "broll_concat_list.txt"
    segment_files: List[Path] = []

    print("\n=== Creating normalized segments ===")
    for idx, (clip_path, seg_d) in enumerate(segments):
        seg_out = temp_dir / f"seg_{idx:03d}.mp4"
        print(f"Segment {idx+1}/{len(segments)}: {clip_path.name} -> {seg_out.name} ({seg_d:.2f}s)")
        segment_files.append(seg_out)

        cmd = [
            str(FFMPEG_EXE),
            "-y",
            "-i", str(clip_path),
            "-t", f"{seg_d:.3f}",
            "-vf",
            (
                "scale=1920:1080:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"
                "setsar=1,"
                "pad=1920:1080:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,"
                "format=yuv420p"
            ),
            "-r", "30",
            "-c:v", "libx264",
            "-preset", "fast",
            "-crf", "20",
            "-an",  # strip any audio from the b-roll segment
            str(seg_out),
        ]
        run_cmd(cmd)

    # Write concat list
    with temp_concat_list.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for seg in segment_files:
            f.write(f"file '{seg.as_posix()}'\n")

    temp_video = VIDEO_DIR / "broll_temp.mp4"

    print("\n=== Concatenating segments ===")
    concat_cmd = [
        str(FFMPEG_EXE),
        "-y",
        "-f", "concat",
        "-safe", "0",
        "-i", str(temp_concat_list),
        "-c:v", "copy",
        str(temp_video),
    ]
    run_cmd(concat_cmd)
    print(f"Temp concatenated video: {temp_video}")

    # Final mux with audio
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    base_name = audio_path.stem
    out_path = VIDEO_DIR / f"{base_name}_broll_{timestamp}.mp4"

    print("\n=== Muxing audio + concatenated video ===")
    mux_cmd = [
        str(FFMPEG_EXE),
        "-y",
        "-i", str(temp_video),   # 0 = b-roll video only
        "-i", str(audio_path),   # 1 = narration audio
        "-map", "0:v:0",
        "-map", "1:a:0",
        "-c:v", "copy",
        "-c:a", "aac",
        "-shortest",
        str(out_path),
    ]
    run_cmd(mux_cmd)

    print(f"\nSaved final video to: {out_path}")
    print("=== Done ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Assistant

Good question, and you’re *almost* right, but there’s a subtle thing here that saves us.

Short answer:  
**No, it will not just keep reusing the same clips every new video**—because `usage_count` is stored in `broll_manifest.json` and keeps increasing across runs, and we sort by that.

Let’s walk it through with an example.

---

### How it actually behaves across multiple videos

Say you have 10 clips: `c1` … `c10`.

#### Before you ever run the script

- Manifest (usage_count for all):
  - `c1`–`c10` → `usage_count = 0`

On a run, in `pick_segments_for_audio`:

1. We build `clip_entries` from manifest:
   ```python
   clip_entries = [
       {"rel": "BROLL/c1.mp4", "usage_count": 0},
       ...,
       {"rel": "BROLL/c10.mp4", "usage_count": 0},
   ]
   ```

2. We `random.shuffle(clip_entries)` → random order, but still all `usage_count = 0`.

3. Then we `sort` by `usage_count`:
   ```python
   clip_entries.sort(key=lambda c: c["usage_count"])
   ```
   - Since they’re all 0, **the shuffle decides the order among equals**.
   - Python sort is stable, so the randomized order between equal `usage_count`s is preserved.

4. We now walk this randomized, equally-used list and pick enough clips to fill the audio length, and we track `used_this_video` so we don’t reuse any clip **within** this single video.

5. After the segments are chosen, we increment `usage_count` for the clips we used:
   ```python
   clips_meta[rel]["usage_count"] += 1
   ```
   and save that back to `broll_manifest.json`.

So after **video 1**:

- Maybe we used `c1`–`c5`.
- Manifest now:
  - `c1`–`c5` → `usage_count = 1`
  - `c6`–`c10` → `usage_count = 0`

#### When you create **video 2** (new script, new audio)

We load the manifest again:

- `c6`–`c10` are 0
- `c1`–`c5` are 1

We shuffle, then sort by `usage_count`:

- All the `0` clips (`c6`–`c10`) come **first**.
- Then come the `1` clips (`c1`–`c5`).

Result:  
For the second video, the script will **prefer all the 0-use clips first**, only touching the 1-use clips if it needs extra footage to fill the audio duration.

Over time, this means:

- It will try to bring every clip up to `usage_count = 1` before any go to `2`.
- Then it will try to bring every clip up to `2` before any go to `3`, etc.

So it *balances* usage across videos. It does **not** reset usage per video; `usage_count` lives across runs.

---

### Where you *might* see repeated clips

You *will* see repeats if:

1. Your audio is longer than the total time available from all clips (with the `MAX_SEGMENT_SECONDS` cap). Then the script errors, or if we changed behavior, it would have to reuse.
2. You just don’t have many clips, so after a few videos they’re all at the same `usage_count` again—and at that point, they’re equally likely, just shuffled each time.

---

If you want even stronger guarantees like:

- “Don’t reuse clips from the **last N videos** at all”  
or
- “Don’t ever let a clip go above usage_count 3”

we can absolutely tweak `pick_segments_for_audio` to add that logic. But as written, it already **doesn’t** “start over at zero each video”—it keeps a running tally and rotates clips fairly.

## User

"""
youtube_upload.py

Uploads the latest rendered video in 07_VIDEO to YouTube using the
matching *_YOUTUBE_*.txt metadata file (title + description).

Behavior:
- Finds the newest .mp4 in 07_VIDEO
- Finds the newest *_YOUTUBE_*.txt in 07_VIDEO
- Parses:
    Title:
      ...
    Description:
      ...
    Video file:
      ...
- Authenticates with YouTube (Desktop OAuth)
- Uploads the video as UNLISTED (you can change this to 'public')
- Prints the YouTube video URL

Usage (from MC_Factory root, in .mc_env):

    (.mc_env) python 04_SCRIPTS/youtube_upload.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Tuple

from googleapiclient.discovery import build
from googleapiclient.errors import HttpError
from googleapiclient.http import MediaFileUpload

from google_auth_oauthlib.flow import InstalledAppFlow
from google.auth.transport.requests import Request
import google.auth.exceptions
import pickle

# -------- Paths & constants --------

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
VIDEO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "07_VIDEO"

# Where we store the OAuth token once you've logged in once
TOKEN_PATH = BASE_DIR / "youtube_token.pickle"
CLIENT_SECRET_PATH = BASE_DIR / "client_secret_youtube.json"

# YouTube scope for uploading videos
SCOPES = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload"]


# -------- Helpers to find files --------

def find_latest_video() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not VIDEO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    videos = sorted(
        [p for p in VIDEO_DIR.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".mp4"],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return videos[0] if videos else None


def find_latest_meta() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not VIDEO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    metas = sorted(
        [
            p for p in VIDEO_DIR.iterdir()
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".txt"
            and "_YOUTUBE_" in p.name
        ],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return metas[0] if metas else None


def parse_meta_file(meta_path: Path) -> Tuple[str, str, Optional[str]]:
    """
    Expect a structure like:

    Title:
    Some Title Here

    Description:
    Long description...
    (multiple lines)

    Video file:
    somefile.mp4
    """
    text = meta_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def extract_block(label: str) -> str:
        pattern = rf"{label}:\s*(.*?)\n(?:\n|$)"
        # DOTALL so '.' matches newlines; non-greedy so it stops at first blank line
        m = re.search(pattern, text, flags=re.DOTALL)
        if not m:
            return ""
        return m.group(1).strip()

    title = extract_block("Title")
    description = extract_block("Description")
    video_file = extract_block("Video file")

    if not title:
        title = "Untitled Materialist Christianity Video"

    if not description:
        description = (
            "This is part of the ongoing Materialist Christianity project. "
            "We take Christ, the Bible, and the working class seriously."
        )

    return title, description, video_file or None


# -------- YouTube auth & upload --------

def get_authenticated_service():
    """
    Return an authenticated YouTube API client.
    Uses Desktop OAuth. First run will open a browser window.
    """
    import google.auth

    creds = None

    # Load existing token if present
    if TOKEN_PATH.exists():
        with TOKEN_PATH.open("rb") as token_file:
            creds = pickle.load(token_file)

    # If no valid creds, do the OAuth dance
    if not creds or not creds.valid:
        if creds and creds.expired and creds.refresh_token:
            try:
                creds.refresh(Request())
            except google.auth.exceptions.RefreshError:
                creds = None

        if not creds:
            if not CLIENT_SECRET_PATH.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"client_secret_youtube.json not found at {CLIENT_SECRET_PATH}.\n"
                    "Download the OAuth client JSON from Google Cloud and save it there."
                )
            flow = InstalledAppFlow.from_client_secrets_file(
                str(CLIENT_SECRET_PATH),
                SCOPES,
            )
            creds = flow.run_local_server(port=0)

        # Save the token for next time
        with TOKEN_PATH.open("wb") as token_file:
            pickle.dump(creds, token_file)

    return build("youtube", "v3", credentials=creds)


def upload_video(youtube, video_path: Path, title: str, description: str) -> str:
    """
    Upload the given video to YouTube.

    Returns:
        The video ID (string).
    """
    body = {
        "snippet": {
        "title": title,
        "description": description,
        "categoryId": "27",
        "channelId": "UCJnd-HDp21jGGERwDfYA4WA"
},
        "status": {
            "privacyStatus": "unlisted",  # change to 'public' when you're ready
            "selfDeclaredMadeForKids": False,
        },
    }

    media = MediaFileUpload(
        str(video_path),
        mimetype="video/mp4",
        chunksize=-1,
        resumable=True,
    )

    request = youtube.videos().insert(
        part="snippet,status",
        body=body,
        media_body=media,
    )

    print(f"Uploading {video_path.name} to YouTube...")
    response = None
    while response is None:
        status, response = request.next_chunk()
        if status:
            print(f"Upload progress: {int(status.progress() * 100)}%")

    if "id" not in response:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected response from YouTube API: {response}")

    video_id = response["id"]
    print(f"Upload complete! Video ID: {video_id}")
    return video_id


def main():
    print("=== YouTube Uploader ===")

    video_path = find_latest_video()
    if not video_path:
        print("ERROR: No .mp4 files found in 07_VIDEO.")
        return

    meta_path = find_latest_meta()
    if not meta_path:
        print("ERROR: No *_YOUTUBE_*.txt metadata file found in 07_VIDEO.")
        return

    print(f"Latest video: {video_path.name}")
    print(f"Using metadata: {meta_path.name}")

    title, description, meta_video_name = parse_meta_file(meta_path)

    if meta_video_name and meta_video_name != video_path.name:
        print(
            "WARNING: Metadata 'Video file' does not match latest .mp4 name.\n"
            f"  Meta file says: {meta_video_name}\n"
            f"  Latest video is: {video_path.name}\n"
            "Proceeding with latest video anyway..."
        )

    try:
        youtube = get_authenticated_service()
    except Exception as e:
        print("ERROR: Failed to authenticate with YouTube API:")
        print(e)
        return

    try:
        video_id = upload_video(youtube, video_path, title, description)
    except HttpError as e:
        print("YouTube API error:")
        print(e)
        return

    url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}"
    print(f"\nYouTube URL: {url}\n")
    print("=== Done ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

That `channelId` is your **EzraByrd** channel. You don’t actually need to specify this at all; YouTube will use whatever channel the OAuth token belongs to.

Change it to:

```python
body = {
    "snippet": {
        "title": title,
        "description": description,
        "categoryId": "27",
    },
    "status": {
        "privacyStatus": "unlisted",  # change to 'public' later if you want
        "selfDeclaredMadeForKids": False,
    },
}
```

Then do the token reset steps above. Future uploads will go to whichever channel you authenticated as.

## 1. New orchestrator: `mc_pipeline_run_once.py`

Create this file:

`MC_Factory/04_SCRIPTS/mc_pipeline_run_once.py`

```python
"""
mc_pipeline_run_once.py

One-shot pipeline:

1) Find the newest .md script in 01_INBOX
2) Generate narration audio for that script (TTS step - you hook this in)
3) Build the b-roll video from the latest audio (generate_video_broll.py)
4) Create a *_YOUTUBE_*.txt metadata file (Title + Description) from the .md
5) Upload the newest video to YouTube (youtube_upload.py)
6) Log everything to 08_LOGS/mc_pipeline.log and mc_pipeline_status.txt

Run from MC_Factory root (with .mc_env active):

    (.mc_env) python 04_SCRIPTS/mc_pipeline_run_once.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Optional

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

INBOX_DIR = BASE_DIR / "01_INBOX"
AUDIO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "05_AUDIO"
VIDEO_DIR = BASE_DIR / "07_VIDEO"
SCRIPTS_DIR = BASE_DIR / "04_SCRIPTS"
LOG_DIR = BASE_DIR / "08_LOGS"

LOG_FILE = LOG_DIR / "mc_pipeline.log"
STATUS_FILE = LOG_DIR / "mc_pipeline_status.txt"

# TODO: change this to your actual TTS script name if different
AUDIO_SCRIPT = SCRIPTS_DIR / "generate_audio_from_md.py"

GENERATE_BROLL_SCRIPT = SCRIPTS_DIR / "generate_video_broll.py"
YOUTUBE_UPLOAD_SCRIPT = SCRIPTS_DIR / "youtube_upload.py"


# ---------- Logging helpers ----------

def log_line(message: str) -> None:
    LOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    line = f"[{timestamp}] {message}\n"
    with LOG_FILE.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(line)
    print(line, end="")  # also echo to console


def set_status(status: str) -> None:
    """
    Write a one-line status file you can glance at:
    e.g. "OK: processed script_mc-001.md -> video XYZ"
    """
    LOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with STATUS_FILE.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(status + "\n")


# ---------- File helpers ----------

def find_latest_md() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not INBOX_DIR.exists():
        return None
    files = sorted(
        [p for p in INBOX_DIR.iterdir()
         if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".md"],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return files[0] if files else None


def find_latest_audio() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not AUDIO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    files = sorted(
        [p for p in AUDIO_DIR.iterdir()
         if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in {".mp3", ".wav"}],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return files[0] if files else None


def find_latest_video() -> Optional[Path]:
    if not VIDEO_DIR.exists():
        return None
    files = sorted(
        [p for p in VIDEO_DIR.iterdir()
         if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".mp4"],
        key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return files[0] if files else None


# ---------- Metadata generator ----------

def generate_youtube_meta_from_md(md_path: Path, video_path: Path) -> Path:
    """
    Create a *_YOUTUBE_*.txt file in 07_VIDEO based on the .md script.

    Title: first non-empty line (strip leading '#')
    Description: the rest of the file + standard footer
    """
    text = md_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()

    lines = [ln.rstrip("\n") for ln in text.splitlines()]
    # Find first non-empty line for the title
    title_line = ""
    body_lines = []
    found_title = False

    for ln in lines:
        if not found_title and ln.strip():
            title_line = ln.strip()
            found_title = True
        else:
            body_lines.append(ln)

    # Strip leading markdown heading markers
    if title_line.startswith("#"):
        title = title_line.lstrip("#").strip()
    else:
        title = title_line or "Untitled Materialist Christianity Video"

    body_text = "\n".join(body_lines).strip()

    footer = (
        "\n\n---\n"
        "This video is part of the Materialist Christianity project.\n"
        "We take Christ, the Bible, and the working class seriously.\n"
    )

    description = (body_text + footer) if body_text else (
        "This is part of the ongoing Materialist Christianity project.\n"
        "We take Christ, the Bible, and the working class seriously.\n"
    )

    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    meta_name = f"{video_path.stem}_YOUTUBE_{timestamp}.txt"
    meta_path = VIDEO_DIR / meta_name

    meta_text = (
        "Title:\n"
        f"{title}\n\n"
        "Description:\n"
        f"{description}\n\n"
        "Video file:\n"
        f"{video_path.name}\n"
    )

    meta_path.write_text(meta_text, encoding="utf-8")
    log_line(f"Generated YouTube metadata: {meta_path.name}")
    return meta_path


# ---------- Subprocess wrappers ----------

def run_script(script_path: Path, args: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    if args is None:
        args = []
    cmd = ["python", str(script_path)] + args
    log_line(f"Running: {' '.join(cmd)}")
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        log_line("STDOUT:\n" + result.stdout)
        log_line("STDERR:\n" + result.stderr)
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Script {script_path.name} failed with code {result.returncode}"
        )
    if result.stdout.strip():
        log_line("STDOUT:\n" + result.stdout)


# ---------- Main pipeline ----------

def main():
    start_ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    log_line("=" * 60)
    log_line(f"MC pipeline run started at {start_ts}")

    md_path = find_latest_md()
    if not md_path:
        msg = "No .md scripts found in 01_INBOX. Nothing to do."
        log_line(msg)
        set_status("IDLE: no scripts in inbox")
        return

    log_line(f"Latest script: {md_path.name}")

    try:
        # 1) Generate audio from md (you plug in your TTS here)
        if AUDIO_SCRIPT.exists():
            log_line(f"Step 1: generate audio via {AUDIO_SCRIPT.name}")
            # Pass the script path as an argument if your TTS script expects it
            run_script(AUDIO_SCRIPT, [str(md_path)])
        else:
            log_line(
                f"WARNING: TTS script not found at {AUDIO_SCRIPT}. "
                f"Skipping audio generation; assuming audio already exists."
            )

        # 2) Find latest audio (should be the one we just created)
        audio_path = find_latest_audio()
        if not audio_path:
            raise RuntimeError("No audio files found in 05_AUDIO after TTS step.")

        log_line(f"Using audio: {audio_path.name}")

        # 3) Build b-roll video
        if not GENERATE_BROLL_SCRIPT.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"generate_video_broll.py not found at {GENERATE_BROLL_SCRIPT}"
            )
        log_line("Step 2: generate b-roll video")
        run_script(GENERATE_BROLL_SCRIPT)

        # 4) Find newest video
        video_path = find_latest_video()
        if not video_path:
            raise RuntimeError("No .mp4 found in 07_VIDEO after b-roll step.")
        log_line(f"Newest video: {video_path.name}")

        # 5) Create YOUTUBE metadata file from the .md script
        log_line("Step 3: generate YouTube metadata from script")
        meta_path = generate_youtube_meta_from_md(md_path, video_path)

        # 6) Upload to YouTube
        if not YOUTUBE_UPLOAD_SCRIPT.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"youtube_upload.py not found at {YOUTUBE_UPLOAD_SCRIPT}"
            )
        log_line(f"Step 4: upload to YouTube using {meta_path.name}")
        run_script(YOUTUBE_UPLOAD_SCRIPT)

        # If we get here, everything succeeded
        ok_msg = f"OK: processed {md_path.name} -> {video_path.name}"
        set_status(ok_msg)
        log_line(ok_msg)

    except Exception as e:
        err_msg = f"ERROR: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        set_status(err_msg)
        log_line(err_msg)
        # Re-raise if you want Task Scheduler to see a non-zero exit
        # raise

    finally:
        end_ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        log_line(f"MC pipeline run ended at {end_ts}")
        log_line("=" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### What this gives you

- **No more “drop and pray.”**  
  Every run appends to:

  - `08_LOGS\mc_pipeline.log` – full text history  
  - `08_LOGS\mc_pipeline_status.txt` – one-line “last status”

- **Titles + descriptions auto-generated** from the `.md`:

  - First non-empty line → Title  
  - Rest of the file → Description (+ MC footer)
  - Written to `07_VIDEO\{video_stem}_YOUTUBE_*.txt`

- **Upload triggered as part of the same process** (calls `youtube_upload.py` at the end).

## 4. Once you find the watcher script…

Open it in VS Code and look for the core loop. It’ll usually be one of these patterns:

### A. Using `watchdog`:

```python
from watchdog.observers import Observer
from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler

INBOX_DIR = BASE_DIR / "01_INBOX"

class InboxHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        # do stuff with event.src_path

observer = Observer()
observer.schedule(InboxHandler(), str(INBOX_DIR), recursive=False)
observer.start()
```

### B. A “while True” polling loop:

```python
INBOX_DIR = BASE_DIR / "01_INBOX"

while True:
    # scan folder for new .md, call other scripts
    time.sleep(10)
```
